upsert.title: Probiome trial: standard bladder cancer treatment plus probiotic or placebo
upsert.center: The Ohio State University Veterinary Medical Center
upsert.status: Recruitment requires confirmation with Ohio State Clinical Trials
upsert.contacts: Blue Buffalo Clinical Trials Office — CVM-ClinicalTrials@osu.edu
upsert.funding: For enrolled dogs, screening and bladder-cancer medical management for 8 weeks or up to 4 rounds of chemotherapy are covered at no cost. Probiotic/placebo is provided at no cost. Limited funding is available for specified treatment-related adverse events. Owners are responsible for cancer care after the study period and unrelated veterinary costs.
upsert.notes: All enrolled dogs receive real standard-of-care treatment for bladder cancer with vinblastine chemotherapy plus daily piroxicam. The experimental question is whether adding E. coli Nissle 1917 probiotic improves outcomes. Dogs are randomized to probiotic or placebo, but the placebo applies only to the experimental probiotic component — no enrolled dog is deprived of standard cancer treatment.
upsert.placebo_note: Placebo is only for the experimental probiotic. Every enrolled dog receives standard vinblastine + piroxicam cancer treatment.

upsert.title: Early-phase rapamycin formulation study for dogs with cancer
upsert.status: Open / current recruitment to be confirmed with Ethos Discovery
upsert.contacts: Ethos Discovery — use the enrollment/request-information form on the official study page
upsert.funding: Study-related examination, bloodwork and study drug are covered; publicly described study support also includes coverage for treatment of study-related adverse events up to the stated study limit. Confirm current financial terms with the study team before enrollment.
upsert.notes: Early-phase interventional oncology study evaluating a novel oral oil-blend formulation of rapamycin, with emphasis on pharmacokinetics, tolerability and dose selection rather than proving anticancer efficacy. The dog remains an oncology patient and continues appropriate real-world cancer care under its veterinary oncology team; study participation evaluates the new rapamycin formulation alongside that clinical care. Do not present this study as evidence that rapamycin improves cancer outcomes.
